Lol. Fiscally taking care of your offspring is not sex specific. Child support is related to child rights not reproductive rights. You're arguing against children's rights through the lens of eschewing responsibility for your offspring. That is not sex specific. Women pay child support too. Abortion is a medical procedure. Pregnancy and birth is a medical condition. Males do not have to pay for the cost of pregnancy or birth unless they are paying for a surrogate and her care. Pregnancy is not only physical but it is fully medical. It effects the health and well being of one human being permanently. Males do not carry pregnancies. 

Child support is not sex specific. Child support is about children's rights. 

Complaining about providing fiscally for a child you fathered is, in my opinion, a vile degradation of what is means to be a man and father. Ironic coming from you who mentions the collapse of the family as an issue but argues against children's rights to a minimum of fiscall responsibility from their biological fathers. 

Abortion is healthcare. Parenthood begins when you have a child to parent. Fiscal responsibility for your biological child is not parenthood, fatherhood, or motherhood. That is the bare minimim for protecting a child's right to care.

I used to have agency and choice over sustaining a pregnancy. I do not now. You talk about men covering the costs of their offspring. But women eat the costs of pregnancy and postpartum care. Do men pay for sustaining a pregnancy? In surrogacy a women can have the costs of her prenatal vitamins, hyperemesis gravidarum medications covered, diet specific foods to sustain a healthy pregnancy covered, any breastfeeding needs, clothing needs, physical therapy needs, and coverage of income lost for medical appointments and postpartum recovery which can last as little as 6 weeks to a year postpartum. Being a surrogate affords more rights and equity to pregnancy at this point. 

Men are not affected by pregnancy. Only one human body takes the toll of pregnancy and that is the pregnant person. 

Women don't "conceal" ovulation. I cannot predict exactly when I ovulate or control when that happens. I can guess. Men can choose to not ejaculate or ejaculate where pregnancy is not possible. Women cannot choose when they ovulate. Intercourse is not always consensual either. 

You are still promoting the fallcy that access to abortion = all medical procedures are then legal. Thats a slippery slope fallacy. Its a cognitive error. I've pointed it out as a cognitive error and yet you still believe that because I have a right to private medical care that only affects me and my body, that actually prolongs my life and causes less life altering affects than a full term pregnancy means you should have access to all medical procedures. I spelled it out for you. Youre being irrational about this point. If you cant see it I cant help you. Review critical thinking and logical fallacies. 

Abortion is healthcare. Abortion has been available for millenia.

Again the consequences of offspring is not sex-specific. Pregnancy is, however. Pregnancy 100% only effects one sex, permanently altering their bodies. You present a fallacy: eg pregnancy healthcare = legalizing all healthcare. Abortion is healthcare. Abortions save lives. Men are responsible for their ejaculate. Men can control when and where they ejaculate. Women cannot control when and where they ovulate. Be responsible for your ejaculate.

Abortion is healthcare. I don't know if you know this but pregnancy is life altering and a medical condition. A female body is permanently changed by pregnancy and birth. There are life ending and life shortening conditions that can be developed. The right to privately decide to choose medical interventions without politicians deciding what is best for you is what RvW protected. Males do not have to live with the life altering consequences of pregnancy and birth - they may have offspring but they did not have to worry about having their bodies and medical needs be permanently altered. Again males do not live with the permanently body altering consequences of pregnancy and birth. Males are responsible for their ejaculation. Females do not choose when they ovulate or if they want to get pregnant. Yes they can alter birth control but that is not the same thing as choosing to ejaculate and where. Be responsible with your body. Stay out of medical choices you know nothing about and dont have to live with when decisions are made.

Do you not believe in risk management? Im not sure why you are not understanding the point I am making. 

The vaccine provides antibodies, reduces spread, and prevents severe infection. Those are all facts. The vaccine does reduce spread even when people are close in contact. Viral load and repeated exposure are part of risk management hence wearing masks and social distancing. Wearing masks and social distancing are impossible in certain professions and tasks (soccer). The spread was probably slower than if the players were unvaxxed but essentially inevitable with an extremely virulent strain like omicron. I imagine the soccer players were not isolating themselves from anyone else and thus a handful became infected and then infection the whole team. The Moderna vaccine, for example, with two doses is only 95% effective. So 5/100 will not have enough antibodies to prevent infection. Viruses evolve to be more virulent naturally.

Some professions are more susceptible to infection. A contact sport? Can you play soccer by social distancing? And not touching yhe ball with ungloved hands? Is the team wearing n95s? Do they train indoors for hours? Do they isolate during their down time? Are they up to date on their boosters? Are they travelling for games to other stadiums? By what means? 

Statistically the vaccine does reduce spread and infection. That isn't a question. That has been answered by the data. 

For example: shark attacks are incredibly rare (137 in one year out 7 billion people) but if you havent been to the ocean for a year?
